Aortic stenosis (calcific): Fixed outflow obstruction → LV pressure overload — LV concentric hypertrophy, myocardial ischaemia, syncope, sudden cardiac death, heart failure — Once mean gradient > 40 mmHg or symptoms develop, median survival < 2 years without valve replacement
Sudden cardiac death: Malignant ventricular arrhythmias secondary to scar, electrolyte disturbance, or severe LV dysfunction — Low EF (<35 %), prior ventricular ectopy, syncope episodes
snip.s: Heart failure: which tests and why

snip.t: Sudden Cardiac Death: Often due to arrhythmias or acute right heart failure.
Haemodynamic: Cardiogenic shock, acute pulmonary oedema, syncope, sudden cardiac death.
Malignant Arrhythmias: Ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation causing sudden cardiac death (highest in HCM and advanced DCM).

ICDs reduce the incidence of sudden cardiac death
in patients with severe LV impairment (ejection fraction ≤ 30%)
post-MI.
Prognosis
Of those who survive an acute attack, > 80% live for a further year,
~75% for 5 yrs and 50% for 10 yrs.
